Synopsis:
The player encounters a dying hyena that is about to turn into a gnoll. If they discover this in time, they can try to stop the gnoll from being born. Otherwise, the gnoll is born and attacks the player when the dialogue ends.

Cluster Contexts:
- PLA_DyingHyena_DeathEvent.json: You’re in the same cave where you already spoke with Rugan, a senior Zhentarim mercenary whose crew was wiped out and who’s desperately holding a gnoll pack at the entrance. Inside the shelter a dying hyena is convulsing and morphing—its body tearing as a gnoll gestates from its corpse. If you discover the change in time you can attempt to stop it (mercy-kill, bless/purge, or otherwise intervene); if you don’t, a gnoll will be born and attack when the scene ends. Rugan’s grim urgency and the gnolls outside make this a pressured, survival‑critical choice that affects your immediate escape and the Zhent shipment objective.
- PLA_DyingHyena_VB_PostFight_1P.json: You’ve just finished a brutal encounter with a pack of gnolls; during or just before the fight you saw grotesque newborn gnolls bursting from the stomachs of dying or dead hyenas. You and a Zhentarim party are holed up (or trapped) in a cave with Rugan, a grim, senior Zhentarim mercenary you’ve already briefed about the missing Zhent shipment, and his priority is getting everyone out alive. The gnoll pack may be led by a flind infected by a mind‑flayer tadpole (its “Voice” can restrain or steer the pack), so there may be a tense psychic element or an option to try risky psionic domination of the leader; time and Rugan’s improvised defenses make action urgent. NPC responses will vary depending on whether the player already knows what gnolls are and on whether Rugan’s companion survived the ambush.
- PLA_DyingHyena_VB_PostFight_2P.json: You and a Zhentarim agent (Rugan, the senior survivor) have just finished a brutal fight with a pack of gnolls at the mouth of a cave; the rest of Rugan’s crew are dead and he’s focused on getting out alive. During or before the fight you saw newborn gnolls erupting from the bellies of dying or dead hyenas, a shocking sight that makes you wary more of further emergences. Depending on prior choices, the gnoll pack may have been led by a flind infected by a mind‑flayer tadpole (creating a tense psychic dynamic) or the pack may simply be defeated and gone. Rugan is terse and practical, urging haste and survival; the player lines here reflect horror at what they saw and a pragmatic caution to watch for more gnolls.
- PLA_DyingHyena_VB_PostFight_3P.json: You and your party have just finished a brutal skirmish with a gnoll pack at the mouth of a cave, during/after which new‑born gnolls grotesquely erupted from the bellies of dead or dying hyenas. Rugan, the senior Zhentarim agent you already briefed about a missing shipment, is holed up in the cave with one other agent (who may be dead or alive) and is terse, desperate, and trying to hold the gnolls at bay—even using improvised fire—so the party can get out. The gnolls may be led by an infected flind (a tadpole‑ridden leader whose psychic Voice can affect pack behavior), so the situation is tense and unpredictable. The player lines reflect shock at the birth‑like gore and a practical urgency to move before the scent of blood draws more gnolls.
- PLA_DyingHyena_Healthy_01.json: A hyena in the plains is displeased when the player is close, wanting to devour them to please Yeenoghu.

context: You’re holed up in the same cave with Rugan, a senior Zhentarim mercenary whose crew was mostly slaughtered; he’s desperately holding a gnoll pack at the entrance while you investigate the shelter. Inside a dying hyena is convulsing and literally gestating a gnoll—its body tearing and contorting—and you have a narrow window to intervene (mercy‑kill, bless/purge, or otherwise stop the emergence). If you fail to act in time the gnoll will be born and will attack as the scene ends, complicating the immediate escape and the Zhent shipment objective. The situation is urgent and tense (Rugan is terse and focused on survival), and earlier events — a brutal fight with gnolls and the possible presence of an infected flind leader with a tadpole “Voice” — can affect NPC responses and available options.
